key_insight: Combustion becomes stable when the flame root overlaps the wavemaker region, indicating that flame localization—not a change in the hydrodynamic instability itself—is the key control mechanism.
engineering_relevance: For swirl-stabilized combustors, deliberately relocating heat release can suppress instability and guide low-emission burner design without increasing inlet momentum.
method: Added low-momentum secondary methane injection through centerbody holes to redistribute heat release.
Used fuel-staging to keep total fuel flow comparable and isolate flame relocation effects.
Applied linear stability analysis to identify the wavemaker region and compare it with flame position.
evidence_signal: Experiments showed a transition from lifted M-shaped flames to attached V-shaped flames, and the stabilized flame consistently aligned with the wavemaker location.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on a specific swirl-stabilized burner configuration, so generalization to other combustor geometries and operating conditions should be validated.
paper_title: Role of flame localization in wavemaker regions on the suppression of combustion instability in turbulent partially-premixed methane flames
